goals.title: Gather stones and sticks
goals.text: Left-click loose stones in the grass and fallen sticks under the trees to pick them up. Breaking leaves shakes out sticks too.

goals.title: Drink a coconut
goals.text: There is no fresh water on this little island. Coconuts hang under the palm fronds: break them down, then hold right click with one to drink the milk.

goals.title: Knap a knife blade
goals.text: Hold Shift and right-click a stone onto flat ground. Pick the knife blade, then chip away the tinted cells with left click (hold and sweep to chip several).

goals.title: Make a knife
goals.text: Open the inventory (E). Put the blade in the crafting grid with a stick below it, and take the knife from the result slot.

goals.title: Cut tinder and fiber
goals.text: With the knife in hand, cut tall grass for dry grass (4), and cattails by the pond or ferns for plant fiber (3).

goals.title: Cut tinder and fiber
goals.text: With the knife, cut tall grass for dry grass, or take palm fronds (break the palm's leaves). A frond and the knife in the crafting grid give three plant fiber.

goals.title: Make a bow drill
goals.text: Three plant fibers twist into twine. Twine and two sticks make a bow drill.

goals.title: Light a fire before dark
goals.text: Shift-right-click a stick onto the ground: that's a fire pit. Add more sticks (each crosses the last) and right-click dry grass to tuck it underneath. Then hold right-click on it with the bow drill.

goals.title: Roast something
goals.text: Right-click a mushroom, turnip or cattail root onto the burning fire. Take it off with an empty hand before it chars.

goals.title: Fell a tree
goals.text: Knap an axe head, put it on a stick, and chop a trunk: the whole tree comes down. Split logs into firewood in the grid (log + axe) - firewood keeps a fire going for hours.

goals.title: Float a raft
goals.text: Two logs and twine lash into a raft section. Right-click the sea with it, then right-click the water beside it to lash on more. Stand on it - it holds you up.

goals.title: Paddle to another island
goals.text: Firewood above a stick makes a paddle. On the raft, hold right click to paddle the way you look. The wooded isle nearby has fresh water and clay; the rocky one, flint.

goals.title: Boil sea water fresh
goals.text: The sea is salt. Fill a fired pot with sea water, set it on a fire and let it boil: the salt stays behind. Ladle it out with a bowl, or fill a waterskin.

goals.title: Hunt
goals.text: Crabs scuttle on the beaches, junglefowl and goats live on the bigger isles. Knap a spear point and lash it to two sticks: it strikes hard and from further away. Roast what you catch.

goals.title: Bring an animal home
goals.text: Right-click a junglefowl or goat with twine to lead it. It follows you onto your raft and off again; let it go where you want it to live. Feed two of them by hand and they'll have young.

goals.title: Shape a clay bowl
goals.text: Dig blue clay at the pond's banks (a shovel is quicker). Shift-right-click clay onto the ground, choose the bowl and build it layer by layer.

goals.title: Fire it in a pit kiln
goals.text: Dig a hole one block deep. Shift-right-click the raw bowl into it, cover it with 4 dry grass and 6 sticks, and light it. Fired in a pit, nothing cracks.

goals.title: Plant a garden
goals.text: Knap a hoe head and make a hoe. Till soil near the pond, and sow turnip or flax seeds (from the wild plants).

goals.title: Make a bed
goals.text: Four dry grass make thatch; three thatch in a row make a straw bed. Sleep on it at night - and that's where you wake if you die.

goals.title: Make stew
goals.text: Shape and fire a cooking pot and a bowl. Fill the pot at the pond, set it on a fire, add food, and ladle the stew out with the bowl.

goals.title: Live here for ten days
goals.text: Keep fed, watered and warm. Build a shelter, keep a garden, keep the fire going.

first_pottery.text: The first pottery has been fired.

pages.title: Getting around
pages.body:
[b]Move[/b] W A S D, [b]jump[/b] Space, [b]sprint[/b] Ctrl, [b]sneak[/b] Shift. Sneaking keeps you from walking off an edge - useful on a floating island.

[b]Left click[/b] breaks what you look at (hold it), or chips and shapes work on the ground. [b]Right click[/b] uses or places what you hold. [b]Shift + right click[/b] sets things down on the ground: a stone to knap, clay to shape, a stick to start a fire pit, anything else to leave there.

[b]E[/b] inventory and crafting  ·  [b]H[/b] this handbook (over an item in the inventory: its page)  ·  [b]1-9[/b] or the wheel: hotbar (over an inventory slot: swap it there)  ·  [b]Q[/b] drop one (Ctrl+Q: the stack)  ·  [b]C[/b] sit down for a close look at your work  ·  [b]V[/b] third person  ·  [b]F[/b] clay brush / knapping flakes  ·  [b]T[/b] chat  ·  [b]F1[/b] hide the HUD

Hold right click to keep going: eating one thing after another, laying stick after stick on a fire.

What you look at, and what each button will do with it, is written under the crosshair.

pages.title: Food, water and warmth
pages.body:
Four bars: [b]health[/b], [b]food[/b], [b]water[/b] and [b]warmth[/b].

Drink at the pond (hold right click on the water with an empty hand) or from a [item:bowl] of water.

The island's water is [b]finite[/b]. Dig beside the pond and it runs into the hole and the pond goes down; open it to the edge and it pours away into the sky. Each bowl you fill takes a little. Rain tops the pond up and fills hollows; thin puddles dry in the sun. Eat by holding right click with food in your hand; roasted food fills you far more than raw.

Nights are cold. Out in the open your warmth drains away; next to a fire it comes back fast. A roof over your head and walls around you keep the wind off. Rain soaks you and makes it colder.

If you die, everything you carried stays in a bag where you fell; walk to it and right-click it. Fall into the abyss and the bag waits at the edge you went over.

pages.title: The island
pages.body:
Everything you need is already here: loose stones and flint (most of the flint lies near the rocky knoll in the north-east), fallen sticks under the trees, tall grass, cattails at the pond, blue clay in the pond's banks, wild turnips and flax, berry bushes and mushrooms.

Trees grow back from [item:sapling_oak]s, berry bushes fruit again every day or two, grass and mushrooms come back. Stone does not: don't waste it.

There is a little cave in the knoll - shelter for a first night. Across the gap to the north-east is a smaller island; you'll need to build your way over.

pages.title: The islands
pages.body:
You wake on a small island in a wide sea, with others all around - none of them big, each a different kind, each with things the others lack. Their outlines show on the horizon: steer for them.

[b]Home[/b] - palms, coconuts, a few stones and sticks, crabs on the beach.
[b]Atolls[/b] - sandbar rings of palms and coconuts.
[b]Wooded isles[/b] - oak and birch, berries, mushrooms, a fresh pond with clay in its banks, junglefowl.
[b]Rocky isles[/b] - granite knolls with loose stones, [item:flint] and gravel; wild goats.
[b]Marshes[/b] - low and wet: clay under the turf, ponds, cattails and flax.
[b]Meadows[/b] - grass hills with wild turnips and flax, berries, goats and junglefowl.

Trees grow back from saplings; a [item:coconut] pressed into the sand (Shift + right click) grows a palm. Stone doesn't come back.

pages.title: Rafts
pages.body:
Two logs and [item:twine] lash into a [item:raft_floor]. Right-click the sea with it to float it; right-click the water beside the raft (or the raft's edge) to lash on another. A raft can be built out twelve sections each way.

Stand on it: it carries you, and you can build on its deck like on the ground - walls, a roof, torches, a bed.

[b]Paddle[/b]: hold right click with a [item:paddle] on the raft: it goes the way you look. Paddle on one side and it turns. Small rafts paddle quicker.
[b]Sail[/b]: set a [item:sail] on the deck and right-click it to raise it. The wind pushes a raised sail - more sails, more speed. Furl it to stop.
[b]Steering oar[/b]: set a [item:steering_oar] at the back, facing forward, and right-click it to take the helm. A and D steer; at the helm you can hold a course across the wind (never into it). W, S or Space lets go.
[b]Anchor[/b]: right-click an [item:anchor] on the deck to drop it, and the raft stays put.

A raft grounds in the shallows rather than running up the beach. Take it apart with an axe, piece by piece - but never so it falls in two.

pages.title: Water at sea
pages.body:
The sea is salt: drinking it makes you thirstier.

[b]Coconuts[/b] are fresh water where there is none: break them down from under the palm fronds and hold right click to drink.
[b]Ponds[/b] on the wooded isles and marshes are fresh.
[b]Boil it[/b]: fill a fired [item:pot] with sea water (right-click the sea with it), set it on a burning fire, and wait. Steam rises, the salt stays behind, and it's fresh. Drink from the pot, ladle it into [item:bowl]s, or fill a waterskin.

A [item:waterskin] (a goat [item:hide] and twine) holds four long drinks: fill it at a pond or from a pot of boiled water, and take it to sea.

pages.title: Swimming
pages.body:
In the water you float with your head up. Space swims up, Shift dives. Under water you hold your breath - the bar shows how long you have left; run out and you start to drown.

To climb out onto a bank or a raft, swim against it holding Space.

Seaweed grows in the shallows. Things dropped in the sea float.

pages.title: Animals
pages.body:
[b]Crabs[/b] scuttle sideways on the beaches. [b]Junglefowl[/b] peck about the wooded isles and meadows and lay [item:egg]s where they live. [b]Wild goats[/b] keep to the rocky isles and meadows.

They run from you if you come too close - slower and sneaking helps. Hunting: left-click them. A [item:spear] (a knapped spear point on two sticks) strikes hardest and reaches furthest; a knife does. Crabs give [item:crab_raw], junglefowl and goats [item:meat_raw] (and goats a [item:hide]). Roast it.

[b]Leading[/b]: right-click a junglefowl or goat with [item:twine] to tie a lead on it. It follows you - onto your raft, across the sea and off again on another island. Right-click it again to let it go: where you let it go is its new home.

[b]Young[/b]: feed two grown animals by hand (junglefowl like seeds and berries, goats dry grass, fronds and seaweed). Two fed together have a young one, which grows up in two days.

Hunted-out islands slowly fill again, while no one is there.

pages.title: Knapping
pages.body:
Hold Shift and right-click a [item:stone] or [item:flint] onto flat ground (the top of a block with nothing above it). Choose what to make: a knife blade, an axe head, a shovel head or a hoe head.

The stone lies there as a grid of little cells. The shape that stays is bright; the waste is dark. Only the dark cells [b]touching[/b] the shape need chipping. Left-click a cell to chip it off - hold the button and sweep across cells to chip a row. Once a piece of waste is no longer joined to the shape it falls away by itself, so chip round the outline and the rest drops off. When only the shape is left, it's done and goes into your inventory.

Press C to sit down beside it for a closer look.

Chip into the shape and you'll be warned; do it three times and the stone splits. A blade with a chip or two out of it is a little rougher and wears out sooner.

Flint keeps an edge much longer than granite.

pages.title: Tools
pages.body:
Put a knapped head in the crafting grid with a [item:stick] below it:

[b]Knife[/b] - cuts tall grass ([item:dry_grass]), cattails, ferns and flax ([item:plant_fiber]); also clears leaves quickly.
[b]Axe[/b] - fells a whole tree at once, and splits logs into [item:firewood] in the grid.
[b]Shovel[/b] - digs soil, clay, sand and gravel quickly.
[b]Hoe[/b] - right-click soil to till it for planting.

Tools wear out with use; the bar under the icon shows how much is left.

pages.title: The crafting grid
pages.body:
Open the inventory with E. Put things in the 3 x 3 grid; if they make something, it shows in the result slot - click it to make it (shift-click makes as many as you can).

[b]Twine[/b]: three plant fiber.  [b]Bow drill[/b]: twine and two sticks.  [b]Torches[/b]: dry grass above a stick.  [b]Firewood[/b]: a log and an axe.  [b]Thatch[/b]: four dry grass in a square.  [b]Straw bed[/b]: three thatch in a row.  [b]Fired bricks[/b]: four bricks in a square.

Every item's own page (at the bottom of the list) says how it's made and what it's for.

pages.title: Building a fire pit
pages.body:
Hold Shift and right-click a [item:stick] onto the ground: a ring of stones appears with the stick across it. Right-click more sticks onto it - each lies across the last: two make an X, four a star, up to eight.

Fire starts from [b]tinder[/b]: right-click [item:dry_grass] onto the pit and it's tucked into the middle, underneath the sticks. (You can also start the pit with the dry grass and lay the sticks over it.)

Then hold right click on it with a [item:firestarter]. After a few seconds of drilling the tinder catches, then the sticks.

A burning [item:torch_lit] lights a fire pit at once.

pages.title: Keeping a fire
pages.body:
Tinder flares for a few seconds; sticks burn for a few minutes; [item:firewood] burns for an hour and a half each and gives the most heat. Lay firewood on top - it only catches from burning sticks, not from tinder alone.

Add fuel while it burns by right-clicking sticks or firewood onto it. When it burns out, a bed of ash is left: add tinder and sticks and light it again.

Rain drowns an open fire unless firewood is burning well. Build it under a roof or an overhang.

Standing in a fire burns you. Next to one, you warm up fast.

pages.title: Cooking
pages.body:
Right-click a [item:mushroom], [item:turnip] or [item:cattail_root] onto a fire pit: it goes on a stick leaning over the flames (four at a time). It roasts in half a minute or so while the fire burns. Take it with an empty hand - leave it too long and it chars.

[b]Stew[/b]: set a [item:pot] on the fire, fill it with water (fill it at the pond first, or pour in bowls of water), and add up to four pieces of food. When it's cooked, ladle it into [item:bowl]s. A bowl of stew is a proper meal.

pages.title: Torches
pages.body: Craft [item:torch]es from dry grass above a stick. Right-click a burning fire with them to light them. A burning torch lights the way when you hold it (your friends see it too), can be stood on the ground or hung on a wall (right-click the top or the side of a block), and lights a fire pit or kiln straight away. Torches don't burn out.

pages.title: Finding clay
pages.body: Blue clay lies in the pond's banks and floor, under the turf and sand. Each block gives four lumps of [item:clay]. A [item:shovel] digs it much faster.

pages.title: Clay forming
pages.body:
Hold Shift and right-click [item:clay] onto flat ground, and choose what to shape: a bowl, a cooking pot, a storage jar or bricks.

You build it one layer at a time, from the bottom up. The cells you still need on this layer are outlined; right-click to add clay, left-click to take it away. Clay where it shouldn't be shows red. When a layer matches, the next one begins.

Press [b]F[/b] to change the brush: one cell, 2 x 2, 3 x 3, or [b]copy layer below[/b] - which fills in this layer exactly like the one beneath it, perfect for the walls of a pot.

Each lump of clay is worth 32 cells; more lumps are taken from your inventory as you go. Leftover clay comes back to you.

pages.title: The pit kiln
pages.body:
Raw pottery must be fired before it holds water.

1. Dig a hole one block deep - a pit with earth on all four sides.
2. Hold Shift and right-click the raw pottery into it (up to four small pieces, or one or two big ones).
3. Right-click [item:dry_grass] onto it four times: a mound of straw covers the pots.
4. Lay six [item:stick]s over the mound.
5. Light it with the bow drill or a torch.

It smoulders for three hours. In a pit the heat stays even; on open ground some pieces crack into [item:potsherd]s. Rain puts out an open kiln - fire it under a roof if the weather turns.

When it's done, take the fired pieces out with an empty hand.

pages.title: Wild food
pages.body:
[item:berries] - right-click a ripe bush; they come back in a day or two.
[item:mushroom]s - in the shade under trees; they come back.
[item:turnip]s - break wild turnips (purple tops in the grass); they give seeds too.
[item:cattail_root]s - sometimes, when you cut cattails at the pond.

Raw food keeps you going; roasted food is much more filling.

pages.title: Farming
pages.body:
Till grass or soil with a [item:hoe] (right click). Farmland near water stays moist; rain waters it too. Right-click seeds onto farmland: [item:seeds_turnip] from wild turnips, [item:seeds_flax] from wild flax.

Crops grow through four stages over two or three days - faster on moist farmland. Break them when ripe for the harvest and more seeds. Flax gives plant fiber.

pages.title: Blocks
pages.body:
Most things you dig can be placed again with right click: soil, sand, gravel, logs, thatch, fired bricks. Logs placed against a wall lie sideways.

Sand and gravel fall when nothing is under them. Granite is too hard for stone tools.

A felled tree topples away from you; its logs land along the trunk. A storage jar picked up keeps what's inside it.

To reach the little island across the gap, build a bridge - sneak while you work at the edge so you can't fall.

pages.title: Shelter and sleep
pages.body:
A roof over you and walls around you keep you warmer at night, and keep the rain off you and your fire.

A [item:straw_bed] (three thatch in a row) lets you sleep: right-click it at night. When everyone on the island is asleep, the night passes quickly. You wake at your bed if you die.

pages.title: Playing with friends
pages.body:
Up to four people can share an island. The host's game keeps the island; friends join with the host's address (shown in the pause menu once the island is open to friends).

Everything is shared: fires, kilns, work left on the ground, the storage jars. A friend can feed your fire or finish shaping your bowl. When someone leaves, their things go with them and come back when they return.
